name: meet-notes
desc: Free, open-source meeting recorder and note taker for Windows — local transcription plus LLM summaries. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **One-click recording** — captures microphone and system audio together so remote calls are fully captured
✅ **Local transcription** — Whisper models turn the recording into timestamped text without a cloud account
✅ **LLM summaries** — decisions, topics and open questions extracted by a local model you point it at
✅ **Action item list** — who agreed to do what, pulled out as a checklist with timestamps back to the audio
✅ **Markdown export** — notes in a format that drops straight into Obsidian or a repo
✅ **Live level guard** — warns when mic and system audio are unbalanced before the meeting is ruined
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, models download separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Feature | **meet-notes** | Otter | Teams built-in | Whisper scripts |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Paid tiers | Bundled with plan | Free, OSS |
| Audio stays local | **Yes** | Upload | Cloud | Yes

faqQ: how to transcribe and summarize meetings locally without uploading audio?
faqA: Meeting assistants all want the call uploaded to their servers, which many workplaces forbid. meet-notes records both audio streams on the machine, transcribes with local Whisper and summarizes with your own local LLM. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, and works with any meeting app.
s1: Dark meeting view (#121417, amber #FBBF24): recording indicator with dual level meters, live transcript scrolling with speaker labels, elapsed chip reading 43 minutes.
s2: Summary card at session end: three decisions listed, open questions section, action item checklist with five rows and timestamp links.
s3: Export dialog: markdown template picker, split by topic toggle, attachments folder set, toast reading notes saved with 38 transcript anchors.
